endorsements.quote: Pipeline execution is sequential with mandatory HITL checkpoints at the Risk Stratification and Routing stages.
The system is explicitly positioned as augmentative: it multiplies CHW reach by pre-screening and triaging, concentrating limited specialist capacity on severe presentations.
Responsibility model. The category of “supervisor” covers two distinct clinical roles, with distinct decision authority and distinct liability allocation.
No severe-tier or crisis-tier action is taken on the basis of the system output alone.
Incident response: a single point of contact within the partner NGO is designated as the incident response lead.

Incidents (missed crisis, harmful output, privacy breach, severe model failure) trigger immediate suspension of the affected agent pending review by a pre-constituted incident review panel (clinical lead, technical lead, ethics representative).
The framework mandates regular bias audits using representative Syrian Arabic test sets and diverse annotation teams.

Equity of access. Any implementation must include low-bandwidth and SMS-fallback capability, address shared-device scenarios, and monitor whether uptake patterns reflect or exacerbate existing inequities.

Any abstention is routed directly to a human supervisor with the underlying symptom evidence and confidence score.

unlisted_practices: Construct a Syrian Arabic mental health evaluation corpus before evaluating conversational AI components for that population.
Consult practising MHPSS clinicians in the deployment region before any implementation work.
Design AI outputs to return an explicit abstention rather than a low-confidence prediction, logged as its own outcome category.
Separate pseudonymisation from anonymisation, with linkage keys held by a partner organisation and never co-located with the AI system or its operators.
Verify AI explanation faithfulness before presenting explanations to clinicians, flagging unfaithful explanations in the audit log.
Do not use verification mechanisms developed on English benchmarks for Syrian Arabic clinical input until validated, and drop any that fail to improve abstention-coverage or risk-at-coverage.
Use culturally appropriate, non-stigmatising terminology in all user-facing output of mental health AI tools.
Prohibit persistent storage of data identifying individuals as mental health help-seekers.
Use structured validated instruments in the first deployment version and stage free-text symptom extraction until it is validated against structured instrument administration.
Pipeline execution should halt and escalate to a human supervisor on agent failure rather than proceed with unreliable output.
Maintain complete audit logs of every decision for post-incident review.
